Regeneron-funded and reported, in press at The Lancet but not yet published as of Oct 2026. script.cta: The full breakdown is on our channel: "Can Trevogrumab Stop Semaglutide Muscle Loss? 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean Mass in Phase 2". It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The core numbers are right. Regeneron's 1 Oct 2026 release (via GlobeNewswire) gives lean-mass change by DXA at 52 weeks of −7.3% on semaglutide + placebo (95% CI −8.8 to −5.8) and −4.2% on trevogrumab 75 mg + semaglutide. That is "42.5% lean mass preservation", and 3.1/7.3 ≈ 42.5%, so "the gap of 3.1 percentage points is the whole 42%" holds. The release also confirms: BMI ≥30, a lower-dose part at 25/75 mg and a higher-dose part at 200/400 mg, "in press with The Lancet" (still not published as of Oct 2026), and "not evaluated by any regulatory authority". Its most common side effects were nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and vomiting. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06299098 confirms Phase 2, Regeneron as sponsor (so "Regeneron-funded" is fair), BMI ≥30 for Parts B/C, and 52-week lean mass as the primary outcome for Part C. The joint nutrition advisory exists (AJCN 2025, published at the same time in other journals). It says lean mass includes "muscle and other non-fat tissues" and recommends enough protein plus strength training. The script already has the kidney caveat, the side-effect line and the exact prescriber line. All remaining issues are minor wording or precision fixes, listed below. I couldn't reach the investor.regeneron.com URL (it timed out), so I didn't verify it. The GlobeNewswire copy of the same release is verified.

issues.claim: Side effects were similar to semaglutide alone.
issues.problem: The release gives this only for the lower-dose part: 77% of people on trevogrumab had at least one side effect vs 82% on semaglutide + placebo. It reports no safety comparison for the higher-dose part. Without a number and a scope, the line reads as covering the whole trial.
issues.fix: Narration: "In this lower-dose part, side effects were similar: 77% vs 82% had at least one." List item: "Lower-dose part: any side effect 77% vs 82% (semaglutide + placebo)"

issues.claim: Headlines say trevogrumab cut lean-mass loss on semaglutide, the drug in Ozempic, by 42%.
issues.problem: The 42% comes from Regeneron's own release ("42.5% lean mass preservation"), and the trial used semaglutide 2.4 mg, the Wegovy dose, in people with obesity. Credit the figure to Regeneron and name both brands so no one assumes the Ozempic diabetes dose was tested.
issues.fix: "Regeneron says trevogrumab cut lean-mass loss on semaglutide, the drug in Wegovy and Ozempic, by 42%. Let's decode it."

issues.claim: Semaglutide Lean-Mass Loss: 4.2% With Trevogrumab 75 mg vs 7.3% With Placebo, BMI 30+ #shorts

hold_reason:
Packaging check REVISE: The packaging mostly matches the verified script. Every caption uses the same numbers: 7.3% vs 4.2% lean mass lost, the 3.1-point gap, the lower-dose part, 52 weeks, adults with BMI 30+ and the 75 mg arm. Each one also says the trial was Regeneron-funded and reported, that the paper is in press but not yet published, and that trevogrumab is investigational. Every caption has the prescriber line.

The Instagram caption adds something the script doesn't spell out: which arm had which adverse-event rate (77% with trevogrumab + semaglutide vs 82% with semaglutide + placebo). I opened the Regeneron press release to check it, and it's correct.

There is no body-shaming, no nudge toward restrictive eating, no weight-loss or brand hashtags, and no hype emojis. The protein advice includes the kidney caveat.

One rule needs fixing: the TikTok caption gives the benefit but leaves out the common side effects. Every caption that carries a benefit must carry the side-effect line. It also drops "52 weeks", the lower-dose part and the "lean mass isn't only muscle" point. The YouTube title has smaller problems: it doesn't name the add-on arm clearly and leaves out the population.
approved_by: editor-in-chief (low risk): The fact-checker passed it: the 7.3% vs 4.2% lean-mass figures, the 3.1-point gap behind the "42%", BMI 30+ and the in-press status all match Regeneron's release, and every caption has the investigational status and the prescriber line. The hold was over the TikTok caption missing its side-effect line and the title not naming the add-on arm; both break house rules but don't mislead anyone, and technical QA is clean (applying the TikTok fix is still recommended).
